# Domain reference: HR / Recruitment

Job family covered: Recruitment Officer, HR Manager (RRH), Training Manager, Payroll Manager, HR Director (DRH), HR Business Partner.

---

## Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior / Recruitment Officer | Experienced / HR Manager-HRBP | Senior / HR Manager | Leadership / HR Director (DRH) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mastery of employment law (droit social) | Knows the basics of the Code du travail (French Labour Code) and the applicable conventions collectives (sector-level collective bargaining agreements). | Handles complex cases (disciplinary matters, terminations, litigation), advises managers. | Leads employment-law compliance, anticipates legal risks, manages relations with the inspection du travail (labour inspectorate). | Defines the employment policy, negotiates collective agreements, handles crises (PSE, plan de sauvegarde de l'emploi, i.e. redundancy plan; restructurings). |
| Talent management | Sourcing, qualification, conducting interviews, onboarding. | Leads recruitment campaigns, builds onboarding paths, manages internal mobility. | Defines the talent acquisition and retention strategy, structures career paths. | Aligns the HR strategy with the business strategy, leads the GPEC/GEPP (strategic workforce and skills planning), manages workforce planning. |
| Manager support | Answers routine HR questions. | Advises managers on team management, annual reviews, difficult situations. | Coaches senior managers, intervenes on complex conflicts, manages performance. | Develops the management culture, structures leadership programs, advises the CODIR (comité de direction, executive committee). |

## Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior | Leadership |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data-driven HR management | Tracks basic KPIs (turnover, time to hire). | Analyzes trends, produces dashboards, identifies alerts. | Manages the HR budget, forecasts headcount, measures the ROI of HR actions. | Defines the strategic indicators, presents to the board, benchmarks. |
| Social dialogue | Understands how the IRP (instances représentatives du personnel, employee representative bodies) work. | Prepares CSE (comité social et économique, works council) meetings, drafts the minutes (PV), manages day-to-day relations. | Leads negotiations on company agreements. | Leads the social dialogue strategy, negotiates structuring agreements. |

## Complementary competencies (x1)

| Competency | Description |
|---|---|
| Payroll & personnel administration | Mastery of the payroll cycle, social contributions, the DSN (déclaration sociale nominative, monthly payroll filing). |
| Training & development | Building the skills development plan, managing OPCO (opérateur de compétences, skills funding body) funding. |
| HRIS & tools | Mastery of HR tools (ATS, HRIS, payroll), ability to lead transformation projects. |
| Employer brand | HR communication, social media presence, attractiveness. |

---

## Recommended role-play scenarios

- **Conflict situation**: a manager wants to dismiss an employee for "bad attitude". The candidate must identify the legal risks, propose a structured approach (interviews, formalization, alternatives) and manage the relationship with the manager. Observe: legal rigor, diplomacy, managerial courage.
- **Hiring trade-off**: two finalist candidates for a position, with very different profiles. Present the files and ask the candidate to structure the decision. Observe: method, absence of bias, ability to defend a choice with evidence.

## Red flags

### Red
- Lack of knowledge of employment law basics for the targeted level
- Takes personal positions on individual situations without a factual framework
- No reference to confidentiality or ethics in their practice

### Orange
- Exclusive focus on administration with no strategic vision (for a senior+ position)
- Difficulty positioning themselves in front of a manager (stance too accommodating or too rigid)
- No curiosity about the company's business
